heuristics: The 32-jump Teske r-adding walk with the seed-dependent mix64 partition behaves as an approximately random mapping on the r group elements, so the first Floyd collision occurs within 3*ceil(sqrt(r)) iterations with probability well above 0.39 (Teske; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe). Supported by the exact-walk toy sample in experiment.py at its own scope.
Seed and jump coefficients derived from 512-bit mix blocks reduced mod r have bias below 2^-257 per coefficient; this does not measurably distort the walk.
limitations: Analytic attack with a stated random-walk heuristic; no production-size execution or independent qualification. Toy experiments bound the iteration distribution at their own scope only.
Generic adding-walk rho, not a number-field-sieve estimate, a practical break, or a security bound.
Success probability 0.39 is a deliberately conservative supported lower bound; the toy sample is far higher but does not prove the production constant.
